classification_rule: Classify the decision context before selecting the intervention method; if evidence is mixed, state DISORDER and decompose rather than averaging methods.

contexts.cause_effect: Clear and repeatable; a known answer exists.
contexts.method: Apply proven practice, automate or delegate within an observed process boundary.
contexts.danger: Complacency and treating a changed context as routine.
contexts.required_artifact: process owner, known exception list, context-reclassification trigger

contexts.cause_effect: Discoverable through analysis; multiple good answers may exist.
contexts.method: Use expert analysis and expose dissent before choosing good practice.
contexts.required_artifact: competing hypotheses, expert disagreement record, decision rationale

contexts.cause_effect: Only coherent in retrospect; outcomes emerge from interacting agents.
contexts.method: Run bounded safe-to-fail probes, monitor patterns, amplify or dampen based on observed results.
contexts.required_artifact: probe budget, kill criterion, signal window, counterfactual and rollback

contexts.cause_effect: No stable relationship is available during the event.
contexts.method: Stabilize immediate harm, expose an observable boundary, then shift the work into complex learning.
contexts.danger: Retaining emergency command posture after stabilization.
contexts.required_artifact: stabilization action, harm boundary, handoff-to-complex trigger

contexts.cause_effect: The governing context is unknown or disputed.
contexts.method: Split the situation into independently classifiable parts; do not use an averaged response mode.
contexts.danger: The loudest stakeholder imposes their preferred framework.
contexts.required_artifact: decomposition map, confidence per component, next observation

promotion_gate: No leverage recommendation may be promoted without a context classification, confidence, and matching response mode.
